# Review — iliad-144 (Iliad 23.99–191)

Two passes. Pass 1: units.json (notes first, then Greek → `l`, `l` ↔ `i`, remembered English, quotation marks, table conformity against the Iliad and Odyssey tables and published parts). Pass 2: re-read of every edited unit, then gloss.json (every parse checked against the line). `t` untouched (checked: concatenated `t` equals the packet's lines; `ln` and `p` flags verified against the packet; line count of `l` equals that of `t` in every unit). No modern translation consulted.

Neighbours: iliad-143 ends with Patroclus's speech closed (”) at 23.98, so 23.99 opens with no speech running on. 23.191 ends the part with no speech open; no iliad-145 yet. Speeches in this part: 103–107 (Achilles), 144–151 (prayer to Spercheius), 156–160 (to Agamemnon), 179–183 (to Patroclus). “ on units 4, 37, 43, 62 and ” on units 6, 40, 47, 64 (both layers), `mark` on 4, 37, 43, 62 only. Correct as drafted. Scansion flags: none; nothing to scan.

Units are numbered from 0 by order in units.json; `ln` given as well.

| Key | Sev | What was wrong | What was done |

| νήει, νήεον | med | "unaugmented and uncontracted (= ἐνήει / ἐνήουν)": νήει is the contracted νήεε; for both the augment is simply hidden by the initial η- | parses restated |
| ἱερεύσειν | low | quoted gloss "to sacrifice" after the unit was changed to "slaughter" | "to slaughter" |
| κλισιῶν | low | "hut, tent": the Iliad's word is "hut" (table 2.9, 7.466) | "hut (of the camp)" |
| ἐνόησε (`__broaden__`) | low | "conceived (a plan)": the Greek has ἄλλο, "another thing", not necessarily a plan (table 5.382) | "thought of, devised (a thing)" |

Every other novel form checked against its line(s); all 93 novel keys present, no extras, all `__broaden__` keys exist in known-forms.json, no entry over 230 characters, only typographic ’. Parses confirmed, among others: τετριγυῖα, συμπλατάγησεν (unaugmented), ἔκδεον (unaugmented), ὄρνυντο, ἥατ’, ἀποδρύφοι, σκήλει’, ὀπάσαιμι, κήδεός (gen. sg. neuter), ἑκατόμπεδον (fem. acc. with πυρήν), παρακάββαλον, the broadened ὑπ’/ὑφ’ (tmesis ὑφ’ … ὦρσε), ἐπέτελλεν, ἔλαβε, ἔδυ, ῥέξειν.

## Considered and refused

- **ἄλλως (144) "in vain".** The table has ἄλλως "idly" (14.124) and "otherwise" (11.391, 19.401), but 21.474 reserves "in vain" for ἄλλως and the sense here is plainly "to no purpose". Kept.
- **ἄσπετον ὕλην (127) "boundless wood".** Table 2.455 "boundless forest" is a standing forest in a simile; 7.418 has cut wood fetched for a pyre as "wood". Kept; departure stands in new-renderings.
- **φίλην ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν "dear native land" (144, 150).** Table 2.158 has "fatherland", but the published iliad-117 unit (18.101) has "native land" and 150 must follow it; 145 matches it for consistency.
- **ἐς πηγάς (148) "at the springs".** ἐς is "to", but the sacrifice is at the springs; the English "at" reads truly and the note says what is meant. Kept.
- **ἀγαπήνορος.** Matches the table (13.756, 15.392) in both layers; note says the sense is unknown. Kept.
- **δόχμια/ἄναντα/κάταντα (116) "aslant", "uphill/downhill".** Considered whether the wording is remembered; it is the plain word-by-word rendering of the Greek and the note records that πάραντα is a guess. Kept.
- **τετριγυῖα (101) "gibbering"/"with a thin cry".** Table τετριγῶτας (2.314) is "cheeped" for young birds; "gibbering" is not among the avoided words and a ghost is not a chick. Kept; unit note and new-renderings give the reason.
- **ἀκτῆς "headland" (125).** Table keeps ἀκτή "headland" even though "shore" would read better. Kept.
- **ἆσαι (157) "to have one’s fill".** Table ἆσαι "glut" is said of Ares and spears; "glut" of lament would be harsher than the Greek. Kept; the unit now matches iliad-143's "take our fill".
- **Note 12 "because they will carry the wood back" and note 20 "where the mound will be".** Interpretive but consistent with the scene; no false claim about a form. Kept.
- **ἔπειτα, ἱππῆες "here those who ride in chariots" (133).** Kept: the preceding unit has just mounted the chariots.
- **ὀπάσαιμι `l` "may I give" / `i` "let me give".** Both are true of the optative of wish; table ὤπασαν "granted" is a different tense and sense. Kept.
- **Line 108, 154, 179 and 150 English.** Compared word for word with the published English in the packet; they agree.
- **Scansion.** No flagged lines.
